sourceNote.title: Invoice PDF export
sourceNote.html:
Invoice PDF export

Testing the Export PDF action on the invoice detail page of a demo accounting app.

  • Invoice states: draft, sent, paid, cancelled. Only sent and paid invoices can be exported; draft and cancelled show the button disabled with a tooltip.

  • The PDF contains company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate (0%, 9%, 21%) and totals.

  • Invoices with more than 25 line items continue on a second page with the header repeated.

  • File name is invoice-<number>.pdf.

  • Observed: an invoice with a customer name containing "Müller & Söhne" exported fine, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview.

  • Observed: export of a 60-line invoice took about 8 seconds with no progress indicator.

bodyHtml:
Scenario: Export PDF availability by invoice state

Test case: Export is enabled only for sent and paid invoices

Purpose: Check that the Export PDF action is available for sent and paid invoices only, and is disabled with a tooltip for draft and cancelled invoices.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app is open. At least one invoice exists in each state: draft, sent, paid and cancelled.

Test data: One invoice per state: draft, sent, paid, cancelled.

  • Open the detail page of a sent invoice. Is the Export PDF button enabled, and does clicking it produce a PDF?

  • Open the detail page of a paid invoice. Is the Export PDF button enabled, and does clicking it produce a PDF?

  • Negative: open the detail page of a draft invoice. Is the Export PDF button disabled?

  • Negative: hover over the disabled button on the draft invoice. Is a tooltip shown?

  • Negative: open the detail page of a cancelled invoice. Is the Export PDF button disabled, and is a tooltip shown on hover?

  • Negative: click the disabled button on a draft or cancelled invoice. Does no PDF get exported?

Expected result: Sent and paid invoices can be exported. Draft and cancelled invoices show a disabled button with a tooltip, and no export happens.

Coverage notes: Covers all four states from the note. The note does not give the tooltip text, so only check that a tooltip is there.

Scenario: PDF content

Test case: The exported PDF has all required elements and VAT broken down by rate

Purpose: Check that the PDF has the company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT for each rate and totals.

Preconditions: A sent or paid invoice exists with line items at each VAT rate.

Test data: A paid invoice with at least one line item at 0%, one at 9% and one at 21% VAT.

  • Export the invoice and open the PDF. Is the company logo shown?

  • Does the invoice number in the PDF match the invoice on the detail page?

  • Are the invoice dates shown, and do they match the detail page?

  • Are all line items listed and do they match the detail page?

  • Is VAT shown separately for 0%, 9% and 21%?

  • Are totals shown, and do they match the detail page?

Expected result: The PDF has the logo, invoice number, dates, all line items, VAT for each rate (0%, 9%, 21%) and totals, all matching the invoice.

Coverage notes: The note does not say how totals are calculated, so compare the PDF with the values on the detail page.

Scenario: Multi-page layout

Test case: Invoices with more than 25 line items continue on a second page

Purpose: Check the 25-line-item page break and that the header repeats on the next page.

Preconditions: Sent or paid invoices exist with the line-item counts below.

Test data: Invoices with 25, 26 and 60 line items.

  • Boundary: export the 25-line invoice. Do all items fit on one page?

  • Boundary: export the 26-line invoice. Does it continue on a second page?

  • On the second page of the 26-line PDF, is the header repeated?

  • Export the 60-line invoice. Is the header repeated on every page after the first?

  • Across all pages, is every line item shown exactly once, with none missing or duplicated?

Expected result: 25 line items fit on one page. With more than 25, the invoice continues on a second page with the header repeated.

Coverage notes: The note only describes a second page. It does not say how many line items fit on each page after the first, so for the 60-line invoice check only the repeated header and completeness.

Scenario: File naming

Test case: The file name follows invoice-<number>.pdf, including when the customer name has special characters

Purpose: Check the file name format and how special characters from the customer name are handled.

Preconditions: A sent or paid invoice exists for a customer named "Müller & Söhne".

Test data: Customer name "Müller & Söhne", plus one invoice for a customer with a plain name to compare against.

  • Export the invoice for the plain-name customer. Is the file named invoice-<number>.pdf, using that invoice's number?

  • Export the "Müller & Söhne" invoice. Does the export succeed?

  • Look at the file name preview for the "Müller & Söhne" invoice. Is the ampersand shown escaped?

  • Check the saved file. Is its name invoice-<number>.pdf?

  • Open the PDF. Is "Müller & Söhne" shown correctly, including the umlauts and the ampersand?

Expected result: The file is named invoice-<number>.pdf, and the export of the "Müller & Söhne" invoice succeeds.

Coverage notes: Evidence: an export for "Müller & Söhne" worked, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview. The note does not explain why a customer-name character appears in the preview when the file name format is invoice-<number>.pdf, or how the preview should look. Record what you see rather than assuming a rule.

Scenario: Export of large invoices

Test case: A 60-line invoice exports successfully

Purpose: Check that a large invoice exports completely, and record how long the export takes and what feedback is shown.

Preconditions: A sent or paid invoice with 60 line items exists.

Test data: A 60-line invoice.

  • Click Export PDF and time how long it takes for the PDF to be ready.

  • While the export runs, check whether any progress indicator is shown.

  • When it finishes, does the PDF contain all 60 line items?

Expected result: The export finishes and the PDF contains all 60 line items.

Coverage notes: Evidence: a 60-line export took about 8 seconds with no progress indicator. The note sets no time limit and does not require a progress indicator, so record the duration and any feedback for review.
